scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

M-ENFORCEMENT-DOWNTIME.name: Duration idempotency enforcement remained disabled
M-ENFORCEMENT-DOWNTIME.end_event: set_capture_idempotency re-enables enforcement, confirmed at runtime by SH-OPS

M-TIMEOUT-RETRY-DUP-MATCH.name: Match between gateway timeout retries and duplicate captures

F-01.statement: Gateway config change CHG-77, made by SH-PAY on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging, disabled idempotency_key_enforcement (on→off); rollback has not been executed.

F-02.statement: payments-db duplicate_captures_by_day shows orders_with_2_captures=0 on 2026-09-07/08 (gateway_timeout_retries 121/117) then equals gateway_timeout_retries exactly on 2026-09-09/10 (118/118, 124/124), the date idempotency_key_enforcement was disabled.

F-03.statement: crm-tickets.double_charge_tickets_by_week shows weekly double-charge ticket counts of 9, 11, 288, 301 for weeks 2026-W35..W38 respectively, with order volumes stable (~21000, 20500, 21400, 20900); the jump occurs at W37, the week containing CHG-77 (2026-09-09).

F-04.statement: psp-logs.capture_attempts_for_duplicate_orders shows 0 duplicate orders in 2026-09-01..08 (238 gateway timeout retries, all sent with idempotency key, all deduplicated by PSP) versus 242 duplicate orders in 2026-09-09..10 (all second captures are gateway timeout retries, 0 sent with idempotency key, 0 duplicates from other paths).

F-05.statement: Payments change runbook §4 states set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and that the change is reversible.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-REQUESTER-APOLOGY-FIX.statement: The problem is a customer-communication gap: double-charge complaints just need faster/better apology replies, not a technical fix to the payment pipeline.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFIG.statement: A payment gateway configuration change disabled or weakened idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries, causing retried checkouts to be captured twice.

H-CLIENT-RETRY-DUPLICATE.statement: Checkout-side retry logic sends multiple distinct capture requests (not reusing an idempotency key) for the same order, causing duplicate PSP captures independent of gateway config.

H-HANDOFF-DUPLICATION.statement: Payment capture requests are being duplicated in transit between ORG-SHOP and ORG-PSP (e.g. retried on timeout) independent of idempotency settings or client logic.

H-TICKET-MISCLASSIFICATION.statement: Most 'charged twice' tickets are not actual duplicate captures but customer misreading of statements (e.g. hold vs capture); no systemic payment defect exists.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The gateway config audit log shows payments engineer SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement (on→off) via change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging, and the rollback was never executed, matching the exact mechanism H-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFIG describes.

The payments-db daily data shows orders_with_2_captures was 0 on 2026-09-07 and 09-08 despite gateway_timeout_retries of 121 and 117, then jumped to exactly match gateway_timeout_retries (118=118 on 09-09, 124=124 on 09-10) — the same date CHG-77 disabled idempotency_key_enforcement. This quantitatively confirms gateway timeout retries only produce duplicate captures once idempotency enforcement is off.

Weekly support-ticket counts for double-charge complaints are flat and low (9, 11) in the two weeks before CHG-77, then jump roughly 30x (288, 301) in the week containing CHG-77 (2026-09-09) and the following week, while order volume stays roughly constant; this corroborates that the surge in complaints began with the same event that disabled idempotency enforcement rather than a steady background rate.

PSP-side capture logs show that before CHG-77 (2026-09-01..08) all 238 gateway timeout retries carried an idempotency key and were deduplicated by the PSP, yielding 0 duplicate orders; after CHG-77 (2026-09-09..10) all 242 duplicate orders are attributed to gateway-timeout-retry second captures sent with 0 idempotency keys, and 0 duplicates came from any other path. This isolates the duplicate-capture mechanism entirely to timeout retries missing an idempotency key, with no contribution from client-side distinct retry logic or in-transit/handoff duplication.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-PAY, the engineer behind CHG-77, states the 2026-09-09 idempotency-key disablement was meant to be temporary, that gateway timeouts/automatic retries have always occurred at a steady background rate, and that the presence of the idempotency key is what lets the PSP drop a retried capture (so capturing twice is a direct consequence of the key being off, not of retry frequency changing). This stakeholder account corroborates the mechanism already shown by E-01/E-02/E-04 and confirms re-enabling is a single gateway-config setting that still requires payments-ops runtime confirmation (consistent with constraint K-GW).

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-CS (the requester) restates the original framing — faster/nicer apology replies — as the needed fix, matching CL-01, but says nothing about the payment pipeline mechanism already established by E-01/E-02/E-03/E-04/E-05.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The payments runbook (§4) is an authoritative document confirming that automation may only execute set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and that this setting change is reversible.

U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.question: Will re-enabling idempotency_key_enforcement reintroduce the gateway capture latency issue that CHG-77 was originally meant to debug?
U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.decision_impact: If latency regresses, payments ops may need to pair re-enablement with a latency mitigation rather than a bare config flip.
U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.resolution_path: Monitor capture latency via payments-db/config-audit immediately after re-enabling and compare to the pre-CHG-77 baseline.
U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.safe_placeholder: Re-enable enforcement with active latency monitoring and a documented rollback-ready plan rather than leaving it unmonitored.

U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION-SCOPE.question: How many customers already duplicate-charged since 2026-09-09 need refunds, and who owns that remediation?
U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines whether a refund workflow for already-affected orders must be scoped separately from (or instead of) apology-communication tooling.
U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query DA-CHG/DA-PSP for the full list of duplicate-captured orders since 2026-09-09 and hand to payments ops for refund processing.
U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Compile and flag the known duplicate-charge order list for manual refund review before building any customer-facing communication tooling.

A-FIX-RESOLVES-WITHOUT-REGRESS.statement: Re-enabling idempotency_key_enforcement will stop future duplicate captures without reintroducing the capture-latency problem CHG-77 was meant to debug.

A-STEADY-RETRY-RATE-CONTINUES.statement: Gateway timeout/retry rate will continue at the same steady background level going forward as it has historically.

problem_definition.requested_solution: An AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice.
symptoms: Weekly double-charge support tickets jumped from 9-11 to 288-301 starting the week containing 2026-09-09, with order volume roughly stable (E-03).
orders_with_2_captures went from 0 on 09-07/09-08 to exactly matching gateway_timeout_retries on 09-09/09-10 (E-02).
242 duplicate orders in 09-09..10, all second captures are gateway-timeout retries sent with 0 idempotency keys, vs 0 duplicates and 238 fully-deduplicated retries in 09-01..08 (E-04).
problem_definition.root_problem: A payment gateway config change (CHG-77, 2026-09-09) disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on capture retries; since then, gateway-timeout automatic capture retries (occurring at the same steady rate as before) are no longer deduplicated by the PSP and produce a second real capture, causing duplicate charges that drove a ~30x spike in double-charge support tickets starting the week of the change.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Payments engineer SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on the gateway via CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging, and never rolled it back (E-01). → Gateway timeouts continue to trigger automatic capture retries at the same background rate as before (E-05). → Without the idempotency key, the PSP can no longer recognize a retried capture as a duplicate of the original and processes it as a second real charge (E-04, E-05). → orders_with_2_captures jumps from 0 to exactly match gateway_timeout_retries starting 09-09 (E-02). → The resulting duplicate charges drive a ~30x spike in double-charge support tickets beginning the week of CHG-77 (E-03).; rejected framings: [('H-REQUESTER-APOLOGY-FIX', 'Addresses only the complaint symptom; contradicted by E-01/E-02/E-03/E-04/E-05 which trace the complaints to a technical misconfiguration, not a communication gap.'), ('H-CLIENT-RETRY-DUPLICATE', 'Contradicted by E-02/E-03/E-04/E-05, which show duplicates track gateway timeout retries and the idempotency setting, not independent client-side retry logic.'), ('H-HANDOFF-DUPLICATION', 'Contradicted by E-02/E-03/E-04/E-05; E-04 attributes 0 duplicates to any path other than gateway-timeout retries missing an idempotency key.'), ('H-TICKET-MISCLASSIFICATION', 'Contradicted by E-01/E-02/E-03/E-04/E-05, which show real duplicate captures in payments-db and PSP logs matching the ticket spike, not a reporting artifact.')]

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request (requested by SH-CS) asks only for an AI assistant to draft apology replies, asserting the needed fix is customer-communication tooling rather than a payment-system defect investigation.

hypotheses.statement: The problem is a customer-communication gap: double-charge complaints just need faster/better apology replies, not a technical fix to the payment pipeline.
hypotheses.rationale: SH-CS (customer service lead) only sees the complaint queue (potential_bias noted) and frames the ask purely as drafting apologies, which would leave any real duplicate-capture defect unaddressed.

hypotheses.statement: A payment gateway configuration change disabled or weakened idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries, causing retried checkouts to be captured twice.
hypotheses.rationale: The protected action set_capture_idempotency explicitly 're-enables idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries', implying it is currently disabled or misconfigured and is a direct, repairable root cause.

hypotheses.statement: Checkout-side retry logic sends multiple distinct capture requests (not reusing an idempotency key) for the same order, causing duplicate PSP captures independent of gateway config.
hypotheses.rationale: The H-CAPTURE handoff has UNKNOWN semantic_validity and payload is 'payment capture requests', leaving open whether the shop's checkout flow itself generates duplicate requests.

hypotheses.statement: Payment capture requests are being duplicated in transit between ORG-SHOP and ORG-PSP (e.g. retried on timeout) independent of idempotency settings or client logic.
hypotheses.rationale: H-CAPTURE's delivery_status is UNKNOWN, so transport-level duplication is an open alternative distinct from a config or client-code defect.

hypotheses.statement: Most 'charged twice' tickets are not actual duplicate captures but customer misreading of statements (e.g. hold vs capture); no systemic payment defect exists.
hypotheses.rationale: DA-TKT reflects customer-reported complaints while DA-CHG reflects actual ledger captures; a mismatch between the two would show the issue is perception/communication rather than a payment bug, which would still differ from the requester's blanket 'apology bot' framing in that it requires ticket-content clarification, not generic apologies.

actions.question: Did the payment gateway's idempotency-key enforcement configuration change recently, and when?
actions.expected_information_gain: Confirms or rules out whether a config change disabled/weakened idempotency enforcement, the exact mechanism H-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFIG claims.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If a weakening change is found, it directly points to the protected action set_capture_idempotency as the fix, which requires SH-OPS approval under K-GW; if not found, this CRITICAL hypothesis is eliminated and attention shifts elsewhere.
actions.why_now: This is the single catalog item that literally describes the config/rule change the CRITICAL hypothesis H-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFIG asserts, and it has not yet been checked.

actions.question: Does the charge ledger show actual duplicate captures per order, and at what rate/time pattern?
actions.expected_information_gain: Establishes ground truth on whether real duplicate charges exist in the authoritative ledger, separating technical-defect hypotheses from pure misclassification/communication framing.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If no real duplicate captures appear, H-TICKET-MISCLASSIFICATION and H-REQUESTER-APOLOGY-FIX gain support and no technical fix is warranted; if duplicates are confirmed, it justifies continuing the technical investigation instead of building apology tooling.
actions.why_now: Foundational check: before trusting any technical mechanism hypothesis or the requester's apology-fix framing, the authoritative charge ledger must confirm duplicates actually occur.

actions.question: For orders with duplicate captures, do the PSP capture attempts reuse the same idempotency key (handoff/config issue) or use distinct keys (client-side retry issue)?
actions.expected_information_gain: Idempotency-key patterns in PSP logs distinguish whether duplicates originate from client-side retry logic generating new keys, in-transit handoff retries, or gateway-side key enforcement failure.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: The answer determines which of three competing technical hypotheses to pursue for remediation, each implying a different fix location (client code, handoff/transport, or gateway config).
actions.why_now: This is the catalog item that most directly names idempotency keys, the exact mechanism separating the three technical duplicate-capture hypotheses.

actions.question: What is the weekly volume and content pattern of double-charge complaint tickets, and does it correlate with ledger duplicate-capture events?
actions.expected_information_gain: Reveals whether ticket spikes align with actual duplicate-capture events or are independent, informing whether misclassification or a communication gap explains the complaints.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If tickets do not correlate with real duplicates, it strengthens H-TICKET-MISCLASSIFICATION and the requester's apology-fix framing as the primary driver; if they do correlate, it supports pursuing the technical cause instead.
actions.why_now: This directly matches the mechanism claimed by H-TICKET-MISCLASSIFICATION (tickets misreading charges) and the requester's framing in H-REQUESTER-APOLOGY-FIX, neither yet checked against ticket content.

proposal.summary: The initial request (SH-CS, claim CL-01/CL-03) asked for an AI assistant to draft apology replies to customers complaining about double charges. Investigation of the actual data established a different root problem: on 2026-09-09, gateway config change CHG-77 (SH-PAY) disabled idempotency_key_enforcement to debug capture latency, and rollback was never executed (E-01, F-01). payments-db shows duplicate captures were 0 before CHG-77 then jumped to exactly match gateway-timeout retries after it (E-02, F-02); PSP logs confirm all post-change duplicates are timeout retries sent with no idempotency key, versus full dedup before (E-04, F-04); support tickets spiked ~30x the week of the change while order volume stayed flat (E-03, F-03). The stakeholder account from SH-PAY (E-05) corroborates this mechanism. Hypothesis H-IDEMPOTENCY-MISCONFIG was CONFIRMED; competing explanations (client-retry duplication, in-transit handoff duplication, ticket misclassification, and the requester's apology-tooling framing H-REQUESTER-APOLOGY-FIX) were all REJECTED against this evidence. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only the read-only verification step (verify_ticket_volume_normalization against crm-tickets) shipped now, per the solution design's release_scope and minimum_useful_scope. The protected structural fix itself (set_capture_idempotency, which requires SH-OPS runtime confirmation per constraint K-GW and runbook E-07/F-05) was not executed in this release because the DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two high-criticality unknowns as open verification obligations: whether re-enabling the setting risks reintroducing the original latency problem (VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK), and how refund/backlog remediation for already-duplicate-charged customers would be owned and scoped (VOB-U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION-SCOPE). Both VOBs remain open and are outside this release's scope.
key_points: Root cause established: CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on the payment gateway for latency debugging and was never rolled back (E-01, F-01).

Quantitative evidence ties duplicate captures and the ticket spike precisely to the date of CHG-77: orders_with_2_captures went from 0 to exactly matching gateway_timeout_retries after 09-09 (E-02, F-02), PSP logs show 0 duplicates before vs 242 after with 0 idempotency keys used post-change (E-04, F-04), and weekly double-charge tickets jumped from 9-11 to 288-301 the week of the change with stable order volume (E-03, F-03).

The requester's original framing -- that the fix is better apology-reply drafting (CL-01, CL-03, E-06) -- was tested as hypothesis H-REQUESTER-APOLOGY-FIX and REJECTED against the technical evidence; other alternative explanations (client-side retry duplication, in-transit handoff duplication, ticket misclassification) were also REJECTED.

What was released: only the read-only verification action verify_ticket_volume_normalization against crm-tickets, matching the solution design's minimum_useful_scope and release_scope; this is the only item that shipped.

What was NOT released: the protected action set_capture_idempotency (the actual structural fix to re-enable enforcement), which requires SH-OPS runtime confirmation per constraint K-GW and the payments runbook (E-07, F-05); it was blocked by an open verification obligation, not executed, and backlog refund remediation (SR-BACKLOG-DUPLICATE-CHARGE-REC) was likewise not executed.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, following a DEFINE gate CONDITIONAL_PASS that deferred two HIGH-criticality unknowns to open verification obligations rather than resolving them before release.
limitations_explained: VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK is open: it is unknown whether re-enabling idempotency_key_enforcement would reintroduce the original capture-latency problem that CHG-77 was meant to debug; this blocks the protected action set_capture_idempotency, so that fix could not be executed in this release.

VOB-U-BACKLOG-REMEDIATION-SCOPE is open: it is unknown how many customers already duplicate-charged since 2026-09-09 need refunds and who owns that remediation; this blocking scope kept duplicate-capture-rate verification and backlog refund work outside this release.

Customers already duplicate-charged between 2026-09-09 and whenever the fix is eventually executed are not remediated by anything shipped in this release -- the configuration fix itself has not been executed, only a monitoring/verification step shipped.
Ticket-volume monitoring alone will not show normalization because the actual root-cause fix (set_capture_idempotency) remains blocked by the open latency-regression unknown and was not executed.
Full remediation (issuing refunds for already-duplicate-charged orders) remains unresolved and is explicitly outside the scope of this read-only release.

The structural fix is marked not feasible within contest time overall (feasibility.feasible_in_contest_time=false for the full remedy); only the non-protected, read-only ticket-volume monitoring action could ship now.
